messages:
morgan: Heads up — after the driver rollout in us-west-2 ~2h ago we're seeing a spike of TRTexec / FlashAttention kernel failures on several nodes. Impacting inference-dedicated and a few CI jobs. Logs below.

infra-bot: driver-rollout/us-west-2 finished at 2026-03-14T10:01:12Z :white_check_mark:

morgan: sample error from gpu-node-17: 
```
[W] FlashAttention: kernel symbol mismatch: expected sm_80 kernels, got sm_75
TRTExecutionContext: failed to create execution context: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what(): TRT exec failed: kernel launch failed
```

alex: which driver version did we roll?

morgan: rolled to nvidia-driver 535.54 -> replaced 530.41.03 across the fleet. CUDA runtime on nodes still reports CUDA 12.2.

priya: hmm, TensorRT and FlashAttention builds in our images were pinned against CUDA 12.1 toolchain. Some custom xformers kernels were precompiled for 12.1/sm80. New driver + runtime shows different expected SM ABI, causing PTX->cubin resolution to choose incompatible kernels.

ajared: can we confirm `nvidia-smi` + `cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version` on affected nodes?

morgan: quick dump from gpu-node-17: 
```
$ nvidia-smi
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 535.54       Driver Version: 535.54       CUDA Version: 12.2     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
$ cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
NVRM version: NVIDIA UNIX x86_64 Kernel Module 535.54  Wed Mar 11 09:12:00 PDT 2026
```

emily: also seeing `dlopen` warnings in the model server log where xformers loads `libflash.so` -> symbol lookup error. Likely ABI mismatch.

priya: this is consistent. FlashAttention includes prebuilt kernels that assume specific PTX compute capability ordering. Driver bump can change which cubin/ptx path is selected at runtime. Rebuild of flash/xformers/TensorRT plugins against 12.2 toolchain should fix, but that's a non-trivial rollout.

jared: mitigation plan options: 
- roll back driver to 530.41.03 on canary subset (us-west-2a) to restore capacity quickly
- or hot-rebuild flash/xformers/TensorRT plugins against 12.2 + smoke test then roll forward
- temporarily route traffic to dedicated instances in us-east while we patch

sean: prefer rollback for fastest SLO recovery. Can we canary rollback 5 nodes and validate? I can schedule a window.

ops-bot: queued jobs impacted: 128 inference requests (P95 latency spiked), 6 batch jobs failed. Estimated GPU-hours lost so far: ~14 GPU-hours.

alex: if we rollback, we need to ensure no node-level state breaks. What's our rollback playbook for drivers?

morgan: playbook: 
1) cordon node, drain workloads (`kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets`)
2) apt/yum install previous nvidia-driver package (we keep 530 package in artifacts)
3) reboot node, validate `nvidia-smi` shows 530 and CUDA 12.1 compatibility
4) join node back to pool and run quick inference smoke (small prompt set)

priya: note: some containers use `--gpus=all` and mount CUDA libs from host via `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. If we rollback driver but containers had vendor-specific lib overrides, test carefully.

morgan: starting canary rollback on gpu-node-12 and gpu-node-17 in us-west-2a now. tagging ticket INFRA-2147.

infra-bot: rollback-job/INFRA-2147 created, assigned to morgan, priority: P0.

jared: also open a follow-up to rebuild our custom kernels in a CI job: matrix builds for CUDA 11.8 / 12.1 / 12.2 and for supported SMs (75/80/86/90). Then publish multi-arch wheels.

emily: agreed. Add automated canaries in staging that load the plugin and run small kernels on each SM target. Catches these before fleet driver changes.

sean: rollback results: gpu-node-12 back to 530.41.03, smoke tests passed, inference pool capacity +1 node. gpu-node-17 still in progress (reboot stuck).

morgan: gpu-node-17 reboot hung on systemd unit `nvidia-persistenced.service`, had to force-reboot. Node rejoined, tests look green. We're seeing errors drop from ~25% -> ~3% failure rate.

ops-bot: update: backlog cleared by ~40% since canary. Cost hit estimate updated: ~18 GPU-hours (includes warm-up).

alex: good triage. ACTIONS: 
- short term: complete fleet rollback to 530 in us-west-2 and notify customers (morgan + seans)
- medium term: CI rebuild matrix + publish rebuilt kernels and wheels (jared + priya)
- long term: add pre-rolling test harness that validates kernel load for all plugin combos (emily)

priya: one more note — when we rebuild, keep `--max-jit-cache-size` and explicit PTX paths in builds to reduce runtime ambiguity. Also consider shipping fallback CPU kernel for critical models temporarily.

morgan: creating status page update and emailing affected enterprise customers. I'll update INFRA-2147 with timeline.

infra-bot: INFRA-2147 status: in-progress -> investigating. Estimated completion: 2026-03-14T12:30:00Z.

sean: after rollback completes, schedule a controlled driver rollout with per-pool canaries and the new CI kernel smoke checks added. No full fleet upgrades until we confirm rebuilt plugin compatibility.

morgan: thx all — will post a final summary when fleet rollback finished and we'll keep the rebuild ticket high priority. :thumbsup:
